==English== [[File:Fields below Frocester Hill (1565).jpg|thumb|right|'''Fields'''|360px]] ===Etymology=== {{root|en|ine-pro|*pleth₂-}} {{dercat|en|gmw-pro|inh=1}} {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:feld|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|feld}}, {{m|enm|feeld||field}}, from {{inh|en|ang|feld||field}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*felþu||field}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*felþuz|t=field}}, ultimately from {{der|en|ine-pro|*pleh₂-|t=field, plain}} or {{m|ine-pro|*pleth₂-|t=flat}} (with [[schwebeablaut]]). {{col-top|2|cog}} Cognate with {{cog|sco|feld}}, {{m|sco|feild||field}}, {{cog|frr|fial}}, {{m|frr|fälj||field}}, {{cog|stq|Fäild||field}}, {{cog|fy|fjild||field}}, {{cog|nl|veld||field}}, {{cog|de,lb|Feld||field}}, {{cog|wym|fald||field}}, {{cog|da,nb,nn|felt|t=field}}, {{cog|sv|fält|t=field}}, {{cog|fi|pelto||field}}, {{cog|ast|-}} and {{cog|roa-leo|platu||plate}}, {{cog|an|-}} and {{cog|es|plato||plate}}, {{cog|ca|plat||plate}}, {{cog|fr|plat||dish}}, {{cog|gl|-}}, {{cog|mwl|-}}, and {{cog|pt|prato||plate}}, {{cog|it|piatto||plate}}, {{cog|la|*plattus||flattened}}, {{cog|el|πλατύς||wide, broad}}. Doublet of {{m|en|plate}}. Related also to {{cog|enm|flat||flat}}, {{cog|ang|folde||earth, land, territory}}, {{cog|ang|folm||palm of the hand}}. More at ''[[flat]]'', ''[[fold]]''. Not related to {{ncog|en|felt}}. {{col-bottom}} ===Pronunciation=== * {{IPA|en|/ˈfi(ː)ld/|[ˈfɪi̯ɫd]}} ** {{audio|en|en-us-field.ogg|a=GA}} ** {{audio|en|en-au-field.ogg|a=AU}} *** {{IPA|en|/ˈfi(ː)ʊ̯d/|[ˈfɪi̯ʊd]|a=l-vocalization}} * {{rhymes|en|iːld|s=1}} * {{hyph|en|field}} * {{homophones|en|feeled}} ===Noun=== {{en-noun}} # {{senseid|en|land area free of woodland, cities, and towns; open country}} A land area free of [[woodland]], cities, and towns; an area of open country. #: {{ux|en|There are several species of wild flowers growing in this '''field'''.}} ## {{lb|en|usually|in the plural}} The open country near or belonging to a town or city. ##* {{RQ:Churchill Celebrity|chapter=8|passage=I corralled the judge, and we started off across the '''fields''', in no very mild state of fear of that gentleman's wife, whose vigilance was seldom relaxed. And thus we came by a circuitous route to Mohair, the judge occupied by his own guilty thoughts, and I by others not less disturbing.}} # {{senseid|en|wide, open space used to grow crops or to hold farm animals}} A wide, open space that is used to grow [[crop]]s or to hold [[farm]] [[animal]]s, usually enclosed by a fence, hedge or other barrier. #: {{ux|en|There were some cows grazing in a '''field'''.}} #: {{ux|en|A crop circle was made in a corn '''field'''.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1927|author=[http://openlibrary.org/authors/OL2416183A F. E. Penny] |chapter=5|title=[http://openlibrary.org/works/OL16814587W Pulling the Strings] |passage=Anstruther laughed good-naturedly. “[…] I shall take out half a dozen intelligent maistries from our Press and get them to give our villagers instruction when they begin work and when they are in the '''fields'''.”}} ## {{non-gloss|When coupled with a number (e.g. two-field) used to define types of [[crop rotation]], denoting the number of different [[crop]] types (and possibly [[fallow]]) that are used}}. # {{senseid|en|geology: region containing a particular mineral}}{{lb|en|geology}} A region containing a particular mineral. #: {{ux|en|an oil '''field'''; a gold '''field'''}} # An [[airfield]], [[airport]] or [[air base]]; especially, one with unpaved [[runway]]s. # A place where [[competitive]] [[match]]es are carried out. ## {{senseid|en|place where a battle is fought}} A place where a [[battle]] is fought; a [[battlefield]]. ##* {{quote-book|en|year=c. 1599|author=w:William Shakespeare|title={{w|Henry V (play)|King Henry V}}|section=act IV, scene VI|passage=Tarry, sweet soul, for mine; then fly abreast,
As in this glorious and well-foughten '''field'''
We kept together in our chivalry!}} ## {{senseid|en|sports: area reserved for playing a game}} An area reserved for playing a game or race with one’s physical force. ##: {{ux|en|soccer '''field'''}} ##: {{ux|en|Substitutes are only allowed onto the '''field''' after their boots are checked.}} ### {{lb|en|baseball|obsolete}} The team in a match that throws the ball and tries to catch it when it is hit by the other team (the ''[[bat]]''). ### {{lb|en|baseball}} The [[outfield]]. ## A place where competitive matches are carried out with [[figure]]s, or playing area in a [[board game]] or a [[computer game]]. ## A competitive [[situation]], circumstance in which one faces conflicting moves of rivals. ## {{lb|en|metonymically}} All of the [[competitor]]s in any outdoor contest or trial, or all except the favourites in the betting. ##: {{ux|en|This racehorse is the strongest in a weak '''field'''.}} # {{n-g|Any of various figurative meanings, often [[dead metaphor]]s.}} ## {{senseid|en|physics: region affected by a particular force}} {{lb|en|physics}} A physical phenomenon (such as [[force]], [[potential]] or [[fluid]] [[velocity]]) that pervades a [[region]]; a mathematical model of such a phenomenon that associates each point and time with a [[scalar]], [[vector]] or [[tensor]] quantity. ##: {{ux|en|magnetic '''field'''; gravitational '''field'''; scalar '''field'''}} ## {{n-g|Any of certain structures serving cognition.}} ### The extent of a given perception. ###: {{ux|en|'''field''' of view}} ### A realm of practical, direct or natural operation, ''contrasted with an office, classroom, or laboratory''. ###: {{ux|en|The design needs to be '''field'''-tested before we commit to manufacture.}} ###: {{ux|en|'''Field''' work traditionally distinguishes true archaeologists from armchair archaeologists.}} ###: {{ux|en|He needs some time in the '''field''' before his judgment can be trusted.}} ### {{senseid|en|course of study or domain of knowledge or practice}} A domain of study, [[knowledge]] or [[practice]]. ###* {{quote-journal|en|date=2013-05-10|author=Audrey Garric |volume=188|issue=22|page=30|magazine=w:The Guardian Weekly |title=[http://www.guardian.co.uk/environment/2013/may/04/paris-green-roofs-building-climate-environment Urban canopies let nature bloom] |passage=As towns continue to grow, replanting vegetation has become a form of urban utopia and green roofs are spreading fast. Last year 1m square metres of plant-covered roofing was built in France, as much as in the US, and 10 times more than in Germany, the pioneer in this '''field'''.}} ###: {{ux|en|He was an expert in the '''field''' of Chinese history.}} ### An unrestricted or favourable opportunity for action, operation, or achievement. ###* {{quote-book|en|author={{w|Thomas Babington Macaulay, 1st Baron Macaulay|Thomas Macaulay}}|title=The History Of England From the Accession of James II|volume=1|chapter=IV|year=1848|passage=Penn was without doubt a man of eminent virtues. He had a strong sense of religious duty and a fervent desire to promote the happiness of mankind. On one or two points of high importance, he had notions more correct than were, in his day, common even among men of enlarged minds: and as the proprietor and legislator of a province which, being almost uninhabited when it came into his possession, afforded a clear '''field''' for moral experiments, he had the rare good fortune of being able to carry his theories into practice without any compromise, and yet without any shock to existing institutions.}} ###* {{RQ:Trollope Way|chapter=2|passage=Tidings had reached her of this and the other man’s success, and,—coming near to her still,—of this and that other woman’s earnings in literature. And it had seemed to her that, within moderate limits, she might give a wide '''field''' to her hopes.}} ### {{senseid|en|in mathematics}}{{lb|en|algebra}} A non-[[zero ring|zero]] [[commutative ring]] in which all non-zero [[element|elements]] are [[invertible]]; a [[simple]] commutative ring. ###: {{ux|en|The set of rational numbers, \mathbb{Q}, is the prototypical '''field'''.}} ###: {{ux|en|Whereas a ring has three binary operators: (1) an additive operator, (2) a subtractive operator, and (3) a multiplicative operator, a '''field''' has four binary operators: the three ring binary operators and (4) a divisive operator. (''N.B.'': Only the additive and multiplicative operators are axiomatic. The subtractive operator may be derived by combining the additive and the unary negative operators; the divisive operator may be derived by combining the multiplicative and the unary inversive operators.)}} ## A physical or [[virtual]] location for the input of information in the form of symbols. ### {{senseid|en|heraldry: background of the shield}}{{lb|en|heraldry}} The background of the [[shield#English:_heraldry|shield]]. ### {{senseid|en|vexillology: background of the flag}}{{lb|en|vexillology}} The background of the [[flag]]. ### {{lb|en|numismatics}} The part of a [[coin]] left unoccupied by the main [[device]]. ### A section of a [[form]] which is supposed to be filled with [[data]]. ###: {{ux|en|The form has '''fields''' for each element of the customer's home address and shipping address.}} ### A component of a database in which a single unit of information is stored. ### {{senseid|en|computing: area of memory or storage reserved for a particular value}}{{lb|en|computing|object-oriented programming}} An area of [[memory]] or [[storage]] reserved for a particular value, subject to virtual access controls. ## {{lb|en|electronics|film|animation}} Part (usually one half) of a [[frame]] in an [[interlace]]d signal. # {{lb|en|cricket}} {{archaic form of|en|fielder}}. ====Usage notes==== * In the mathematical sense, some languages, such as French, use a term that literally means ''[[body]]''. This denotes a [[division ring]] or [[skew field]], not necessarily [[commutative]].
